findings.explanation: The settings block repeats the exact same two-line { name = ..., value = ... } shape eight times for log_lock_waits, log_disconnections, log_connections, log_checkpoints, log_duration, log_hostname, log_statement, and cloudsql.enable_pgaudit. A rules engine scores single-resource complexity but has no similarity pass across sibling blocks within one resource, so it can't flag that a dynamic block over a local map/list would collapse this to one place, making it trivial to add or audit a flag later.
findings.title: Eight near-identical database_flags blocks could be a single dynamic block

findings.explanation: The Cloud SQL service agent (service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-cloud-sql.iam.gserviceaccount.com) is not guaranteed to exist just because the Cloud SQL Admin API is enabled or referenced — Google's own CMEK setup docs treat creating it as a distinct, explicit step (gcloud beta services identity create / the google_project_service_identity resource), not something implied by using the API. Building the member string by hand assumes the agent already exists from some prior, out-of-band action. On a project where Cloud SQL hasn't been used before (a fresh project, or one where this is the first Cloud SQL resource ever provisioned), granting an IAM role to a service account that doesn't exist yet fails apply — a rules engine can't catch this because it requires knowing GCP's service-agent lifecycle semantics, not anything visible in the attribute graph.
findings.title: CMEK IAM grant targets the Cloud SQL service agent by string interpolation, with no resource that guarantees the agent exists
